name: Inverted Wide 4-4-2

slots.why: The goalkeeper distributes simply into a compact defensive shape.
The defensive full-back stays behind the defensive winger to keep one flank secure.
The central defender protects the box; Cover is available for a faster player.
The ball-playing defender can switch the counter toward the open right flank.
The attacking wing-back overlaps after the inverted winger moves inside.
The defensive winger forms a protective unit with the left-back and prevents both flanks from being exposed.
The holding midfielder covers the attacking wing-back and protects central transitions.
The box-to-box midfielder carries support into the counter.
The inverted winger attacks the inside channel, creating the outside lane for the wing-back.
The deep-lying forward connects the break and releases the runner.
The advanced forward runs into the space opened by the inverted right side.

description: A 4-4-2 with a defensive winger securing one side and an inverted winger plus attacking wing-back creating a counter-attacking overload on the other.
whyGood: It gives a flat inverted winger a clear overlapping partner without asking both wide players to abandon defensive work.
whyThisShape: The left flank protects the block, while the right creates a three-player attack: the inverted winger comes inside, the wing-back overlaps and the box-to-box midfielder supports. The two strikers give each counter a link and a runner.
whenToUse: When you have a natural flat inverted winger, an energetic attacking full-back and a wide defensive specialist on the opposite side.
whenNotToUse: Against an opponent that can repeatedly isolate the attacking right-back, or when the defensive winger cannot carry his side's defensive load.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Overlap Right: Ask the right-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Full Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
